newsitem.title: UK: LucasVarity off on overhang, press interview.
newsitem.headline: LucasVarity off on overhang, press interview.

text.p: Shares in LucasVarity Plc fell on Monday, hit by an overhang of stock and a Sunday newspaper article highlighting the firm's dilemma over dividend policy, dealers said.
Shares in the Anglo-American vehicle components firm were 7-1/2p weaker at 195-1/2 by 1148 GMT. Dealers said the stock's fall below the psychologically-important 200p level had accelerated its fall.
"There's a fair bit of stock washing around and a lot of people were tempted to get out once the price went below two pounds," one market-maker said.
Dealers said a Sunday Times interview with chief executive Victor Rice had highlighted concerns about the company's dividend policy, which have been weighing on the stock.
The newspaper said the merger between Varity of the U.S. and Britain's Lucas had led to a dilemma on dividends.
"I have got American investors who know Varity for never having paid a dividend in recent years and for being an aggressive user of share buy-backs," it quoted Rice as saying.

"But as an FTSE 100 company, we have many British shareholders who are accustomed to a certain level of dividend payments. How am I going to satisfy both sets of shareholders? I don't have a solution to that."
